note: Help's two lists as K's note of Thursday, November 19, 2026 has them, for every variant of the words.

own=true emailHidden=true pagesOn=true s: One sentence about the club
Say what the club is in one sentence. It shows as About on your club's page, and its beginning shows in search results. You can write up to 2,000 characters.
How the club meets, in words
The days, the time and the place, as the club says them, such as "First and third Tuesdays at 7:00 PM". Keep it short.
Where

The place the club meets, its street if you know it, and a note such as the room. Set the pin yourself: click the map, drag the pin, or paste coordinates or a Google Maps link. If the club meets in two places, press Add another place. To take the second place off, press Remove place 2, then save.
Contact name shown on the page
The person a visitor should ask for.
Email for messages
LCA can reach the club at this address. Visitors never see it.
Name and address
The city shows under your club's name and helps people find a club near them. The page's web address stays the same if the club is renamed, so old links keep working.
Club name, region and page address
Only LCA admins can change these. The region decides which regional representative manages the club.
Cost and who is welcome

Cost: what a club night costs, such as "Free" or "$5 toward the room". Who is welcome: who the club is for, and what a first-timer should bring or ask for. Tick a box only when it is true of the club.
Links
Paste the whole web address, starting with https://, such as your club's Facebook page. Leave a box empty if the club has no such page.
Logo and club color
Choose a picture. It is fitted and saved right away, without pressing Save and publish. The club's own color. A club with none shows navy.
Today's page shows different words here
Your club's page shows different words than this box holds. Saving puts this box's words on the page in their place, so read both before you save.
Save and publish

Your changes show on your club's page right away. If you are not the club's regional representative, the representative gets an email saying what changed. Search results can take a few days to catch up.

One sentence about the club
Say what the club is in one sentence. It shows as About on the club's page, and its beginning shows in search results. You can write up to 2,000 characters.
How the club meets, in words
The days, the time and the place, as the club says them, such as "First and third Tuesdays at 7:00 PM". Keep it short.
Where

The place the club meets, its street if you know it, and a note such as the room. Set the pin yourself: click the map, drag the pin, or paste coordinates or a Google Maps link. If the club meets in two places, press Add another place. To take the second place off, press Remove place 2, then save.
Contact name
The person a visitor should ask for.
Email for messages
Messages for the club are sent to this address. Visitors can see it on the club's page.
Name and address

The city shows under the club's name and helps people find a club near them. The page's web address stays the same if the club is renamed, so old links keep working. To change the name, the region or the web address, ask an LCA admin.
Cost and who is welcome

Cost: what a club night costs, such as "Free" or "$5 toward the room". Who is welcome: who the club is for, and what a first-timer should bring or ask for. Tick a box only when it is true of the club.
